  "title": "Less is more: Which energy efficiency enablers could prosper as AI data centres proliferate?",
  "type": "sector",
  "priority": "medium",
  "published": "2026-09-14",
  "insights": [

   "Hyperscalers are prioritizing computational efficiency to maximize output from existing power allocations, driving demand for advanced semiconductor packaging and memory technologies.",
   "Advanced packaging, including high-bandwidth memory (HBM), is essential to solving the 'memory wall' bottleneck where processors sit idle due to data transfer delays.",
   "Networking is the second-largest power consumer in AI data centers, creating a structural shift from copper to optical networking and co-packaged optics (CPO).",
   "Data centers are evolving from passive power consumers to active grid participants, utilizing on-site battery storage and flexible workload management to mitigate power volatility.",
   "The report identifies semiconductor foundries, inspection/testing firms, optical component suppliers, and battery/backup power providers as key beneficiaries of the AI efficiency buildout."
  ],

  "type": "macro",

  "insights": [
   "Contrary to conventional wisdom, college-educated, high-income, city-dwelling (CHIC) households are likely to benefit most from AI on net, despite their high occupational exposure to displacement.",
   "CHIC households benefit from three key channels: productivity-driven wage growth, significant equity wealth effects, and longer-term disinflation in services.",
   "In the base case, task creation and wealth effects offset labor displacement, resulting in increased output and income, though income and wealth inequality will likely widen.",
   "Younger CHIC workers are more vulnerable to displacement as AI substitutes for entry-level tasks, whereas older, established professionals are better positioned for augmentation and asset-price gains.",
   "In the bear case of rapid AI diffusion, CHIC households experience the initial adverse effects of displacement, but the resulting aggregate demand shock spreads weakness across all cohorts.",
   "Equity wealth is highly concentrated; the top 20% income cohort accounts for 87% of direct consumer holdings of corporate equities and mutual funds.",
   "For high-income households, equity wealth is roughly six times annual labor income, meaning modest asset-price gains can offset temporary labor income losses.",
